output.brief:
The wrong dates did not come from the operators or the printer upgrade. The printer job records show the data arriving from PackBridge already wrong. From 4 Oct 22:10, every Veltranol job carried a 36-month shelf life instead of 24, and no operator overrode anything. Before that, 30 jobs were correct, including three set up by the new agency staff after the firmware change. Two of the 17 bad jobs ran on Line 1 days with permanent staff, and those lots are in the warehouse.

The ERP audit trail explains the trigger. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months for Veltranol under CC-309, valid only from 1 Mar 2027. The current 24-month value is still in force. PackBridge should have ignored the future value but evidently used it. The vendor says it can't do that, and I haven't established why it did.

I'm fairly confident of the cause. I'm less sure of the PackBridge mechanism and whether other products are affected. Two other products also have future-dated entries.

Next steps:
- Drop the warnings and the removal of agency staff.
- Fix the Veltranol ERP records.
- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two Line 1 lots.
- Add a second-person check of the printed expiry at setup.
- Check retained cartons for the two future-dated products.
- Have the vendor and IT explain the PackBridge behaviour.
- Keep the camera check on.
